personae.name: Roman and Volscian Senators
personae.blurb: Patricians, Aediles, Lictors, Soldiers, Citizens, Messengers, Servants to Aufidius, and other Attendants

lines.text: Enter a company of mutinous Citizens, with staves, clubs, and other weapons.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Before we proceed any further, hear me speak.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Speak, speak!

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: You are all resolved rather to die than to famish?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Resolved, resolved!

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: First, you know Caius Martius is chief enemy to the people.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: We know’t, we know’t!

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Let us kill him, and we’ll have corn at our own price. Is’t a verdict?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: No more talking on’t; let it be done. Away, away!

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: One word, good citizens.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: We are accounted poor citizens, the patricians good. What authority

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: surfeits on would relieve us. If they would yield us but the

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: superfluity while it were wholesome, we might guess they relieved us

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: humanely. But they think we are too dear. The leanness that afflicts

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: us, the object of our misery, is as an inventory to particularize their

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: abundance; our sufferance is a gain to them. Let us revenge this with

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: our pikes ere we become rakes; for the gods know I speak this in hunger

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: for bread, not in thirst for revenge.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Would you proceed especially against Caius Martius?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Against him first. He’s a very dog to the commonalty.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Consider you what services he has done for his country?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Very well, and could be content to give him good report for’t, but that

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: he pays himself with being proud.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Nay, but speak not maliciously.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: I say unto you, what he hath done famously he did it to that end.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Though soft-conscienced men can be content to say it was for his

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: country, he did it to please his mother and to be partly proud, which

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: he is, even to the altitude of his virtue.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: What he cannot help in his nature you account a vice in him. You must

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: in no way say he is covetous.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: If I must not, I need not be barren of accusations. He hath faults,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: with surplus, to tire in repetition. [_Shouts within_.] What shouts are

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: these? The other side o’ th’ city is risen. Why stay we prating here?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: To th’ Capitol!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Come, come!
Enter Menenius Agrippa.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Soft, who comes here?

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Worthy Menenius Agrippa, one that hath always loved the people.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: He’s one honest enough. Would all the rest were so!

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: What work’s, my countrymen, in hand? Where go you

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: With bats and clubs? The matter? Speak, I pray you.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Our business is not unknown to th’ Senate. They have had inkling this

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: fortnight what we intend to do, which now we’ll show ’em in deeds. They

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: say poor suitors have strong breaths; they shall know we have strong

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: arms too.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Why, masters, my good friends, mine honest neighbours,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Will you undo yourselves?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: We cannot, sir; we are undone already.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: I tell you, friends, most charitable care

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Have the patricians of you. For your wants,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Your suffering in this dearth, you may as well

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Strike at the heaven with your staves as lift them

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Against the Roman state, whose course will on

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The way it takes, cracking ten thousand curbs

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Of more strong link asunder than can ever

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Appear in your impediment. For the dearth,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The gods, not the patricians, make it, and

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Your knees to them, not arms, must help. Alack,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You are transported by calamity

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Thither where more attends you, and you slander

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The helms o’ th’ state, who care for you like fathers,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: When you curse them as enemies.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Care for us? True, indeed! They ne’er cared for us yet. Suffer us to

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: famish, and their storehouses crammed with grain; make edicts for usury

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: to support usurers; repeal daily any wholesome act established against

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: the rich, and provide more piercing statutes daily to chain up and

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: restrain the poor. If the wars eat us not up, they will; and there’s

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: all the love they bear us.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Either you must confess yourselves wondrous malicious

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Or be accused of folly. I shall tell you

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: A pretty tale. It may be you have heard it,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: But since it serves my purpose, I will venture

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: To stale’t a little more.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Well, I’ll hear it, sir; yet you must not think to fob off our disgrace

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: with a tale. But, an’t please you, deliver.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: There was a time when all the body’s members

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Rebelled against the belly, thus accused it:

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: That only like a gulf it did remain

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: I’ th’ midst o’ th’ body, idle and unactive,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Still cupboarding the viand, never bearing

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Like labour with the rest, where th’ other instruments

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Did see and hear, devise, instruct, walk, feel,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And, mutually participate, did minister

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Unto the appetite and affection common

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Of the whole body. The belly answered—

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Well, sir, what answer made the belly?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Sir, I shall tell you. With a kind of smile,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Which ne’er came from the lungs, but even thus—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: For, look you, I may make the belly smile

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: As well as speak—it tauntingly replied

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: To th’ discontented members, the mutinous parts

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: That envied his receipt; even so most fitly

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: As you malign our senators for that

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: They are not such as you.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Your belly’s answer—what?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: The kingly crowned head, the vigilant eye,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: The counsellor heart, the arm our soldier,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Our steed the leg, the tongue our trumpeter,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: With other muniments and petty helps

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Is this our fabric, if that they—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: ’Fore me, this fellow speaks. What then? What then?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Should by the cormorant belly be restrained,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Who is the sink o’ th’ body—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Well, what then?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: The former agents, if they did complain,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: What could the belly answer?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: I will tell you,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: If you’ll bestow a small—of what you have little—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Patience awhile, you’st hear the belly’s answer.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: You are long about it.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Note me this, good friend;

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Your most grave belly was deliberate,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Not rash like his accusers, and thus answered:

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: “True is it, my incorporate friends,” quoth he,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: “That I receive the general food at first

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Which you do live upon; and fit it is,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Because I am the storehouse and the shop

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Of the whole body. But, if you do remember,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: I send it through the rivers of your blood

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Even to the court, the heart, to th’ seat o’ th’ brain;

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And, through the cranks and offices of man,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The strongest nerves and small inferior veins

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: From me receive that natural competency

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Whereby they live. And though that all at once,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You, my good friends”—this says the belly, mark me—

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Ay, sir, well, well.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: “Though all at once cannot

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: See what I do deliver out to each,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Yet I can make my audit up, that all

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: From me do back receive the flour of all,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And leave me but the bran.” What say you to’t?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: It was an answer. How apply you this?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The senators of Rome are this good belly,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And you the mutinous members. For examine

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Their counsels and their cares, digest things rightly

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Touching the weal o’ th’ common, you shall find

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: No public benefit which you receive

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: But it proceeds or comes from them to you

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And no way from yourselves. What do you think,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You, the great toe of this assembly?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: I the great toe? Why the great toe?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: For that, being one o’ th’ lowest, basest, poorest,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Of this most wise rebellion, thou goest foremost.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Thou rascal, that art worst in blood to run,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Lead’st first to win some vantage.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: But make you ready your stiff bats and clubs.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Rome and her rats are at the point of battle;

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The one side must have bale.
Enter Caius Martius.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Hail, noble Martius.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Thanks.—What’s the matter, you dissentious rogues,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That, rubbing the poor itch of your opinion,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Make yourselves scabs?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: We have ever your good word.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: He that will give good words to thee will flatter

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Beneath abhorring. What would you have, you curs,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That like nor peace nor war? The one affrights you;

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: The other makes you proud. He that trusts to you,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Where he should find you lions, finds you hares;

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Where foxes, geese. You are no surer, no,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Than is the coal of fire upon the ice

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Or hailstone in the sun. Your virtue is

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To make him worthy whose offence subdues him,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And curse that justice did it. Who deserves greatness

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Deserves your hate; and your affections are

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: A sick man’s appetite, who desires most that

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Which would increase his evil. He that depends

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Upon your favours swims with fins of lead,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And hews down oaks with rushes. Hang ye! Trust ye?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: With every minute you do change a mind

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And call him noble that was now your hate,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Him vile that was your garland. What’s the matter,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That in these several places of the city

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: You cry against the noble senate, who,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Under the gods, keep you in awe, which else

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Would feed on one another?—What’s their seeking?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: For corn at their own rates, whereof they say

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The city is well stored.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Hang ’em! They say?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They’ll sit by th’ fire and presume to know

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: What’s done i’ th’ Capitol, who’s like to rise,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Who thrives and who declines; side factions and give out

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Conjectural marriages, making parties strong

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And feebling such as stand not in their liking

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Below their cobbled shoes. They say there’s grain enough?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Would the nobility lay aside their ruth

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And let me use my sword, I’d make a quarry

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: With thousands of these quartered slaves as high

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: As I could pick my lance.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Nay, these are almost thoroughly persuaded;

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: For though abundantly they lack discretion,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Yet are they passing cowardly. But I beseech you,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: What says the other troop?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They are dissolved. Hang ’em!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They said they were an-hungry, sighed forth proverbs

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That hunger broke stone walls, that dogs must eat,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That meat was made for mouths, that the gods sent not

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Corn for the rich men only. With these shreds

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They vented their complainings, which being answered

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And a petition granted them—a strange one,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To break the heart of generosity

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And make bold power look pale—they threw their caps

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: As they would hang them on the horns o’ th’ moon,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Shouting their emulation.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: What is granted them?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Five tribunes to defend their vulgar wisdoms,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Of their own choice. One’s Junius Brutus,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Sicinius Velutus, and I know not. ’Sdeath!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: The rabble should have first unroofed the city

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Ere so prevailed with me. It will in time

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Win upon power and throw forth greater themes

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: For insurrection’s arguing.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: This is strange.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Go get you home, you fragments.
Enter a Messenger hastily.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Where’s Caius Martius?

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Here. What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The news is, sir, the Volsces are in arms.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: I am glad on’t. Then we shall ha’ means to vent

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Our musty superfluity.
Enter Sicinius Velutus, Junius Brutus, two Tribunes; Cominius, Titus Lartius with other Senators.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: See, our best elders.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Martius, ’tis true that you have lately told us:

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: The Volsces are in arms.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They have a leader,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Tullus Aufidius, that will put you to’t.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: I sin in envying his nobility,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And, were I anything but what I am,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: I would wish me only he.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: You have fought together.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Were half to half the world by th’ ears and he

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Upon my party, I’d revolt, to make

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Only my wars with him. He is a lion

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That I am proud to hunt.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Then, worthy Martius,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Attend upon Cominius to these wars.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: It is your former promise.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Sir, it is,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And I am constant.—Titus Lartius, thou

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Shalt see me once more strike at Tullus’ face.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: What, art thou stiff? Stand’st out?

lines.speaker: TITUS LARTIUS
lines.text: No, Caius Martius,

lines.speaker: TITUS LARTIUS
lines.text: I’ll lean upon one crutch and fight with th’ other

lines.speaker: TITUS LARTIUS
lines.text: Ere stay behind this business.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: O, true bred!

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Your company to th’ Capitol, where I know

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Our greatest friends attend us.

lines.speaker: TITUS LARTIUS
lines.text: Lead you on.

lines.speaker: TITUS LARTIUS
lines.text: Follow Cominius. We must follow you;

lines.speaker: TITUS LARTIUS
lines.text: Right worthy your priority.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Noble Martius.
[_To the Citizens_.]

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Hence to your homes, begone.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Nay, let them follow.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: The Volsces have much corn; take these rats thither

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To gnaw their garners. Worshipful mutineers,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Your valour puts well forth. Pray follow.
[_Exeunt. Sicinius and Brutus remain_.]

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Was ever man so proud as is this Martius?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He has no equal.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: When we were chosen tribunes for the people—

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Marked you his lip and eyes?

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Nay, but his taunts.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Being moved, he will not spare to gird the gods.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Bemock the modest moon.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The present wars devour him! He is grown

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Too proud to be so valiant.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Such a nature,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Tickled with good success, disdains the shadow

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Which he treads on at noon. But I do wonder

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: His insolence can brook to be commanded

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Under Cominius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Fame, at the which he aims,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: In whom already he’s well graced, cannot

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Better be held nor more attained than by

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: A place below the first; for what miscarries

lines.text: Shall be the General’s fault, though he perform

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To th’ utmost of a man, and giddy censure

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Will then cry out of Martius “O, if he

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Besides, if things go well,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Opinion that so sticks on Martius shall

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Of his demerits rob Cominius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Half all Cominius’ honours are to Martius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Though Martius earned them not, and all his faults

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To Martius shall be honours, though indeed

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: In aught he merit not.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Let’s hence and hear

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: How the dispatch is made, and in what fashion,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: More than in singularity, he goes

lines.speaker: SICINIUS

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let’s along.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Tullus Aufidius with Senators of Corioles.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: So, your opinion is, Aufidius,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: That they of Rome are entered in our counsels

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: And know how we proceed.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Is it not yours?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: What ever have been thought on in this state

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: That could be brought to bodily act ere Rome

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Had circumvention? ’Tis not four days gone

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Since I heard thence. These are the words—I think

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I have the letter here. Yes, here it is.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: _They have pressed a power, but it is not known

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Whether for east or west. The dearth is great.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: The people mutinous; and, it is rumoured,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Cominius, Martius your old enemy,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Who is of Rome worse hated than of you,—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And Titus Lartius, a most valiant Roman,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: These three lead on this preparation

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Whither ’tis bent. Most likely ’tis for you.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Consider of it._

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Our army’s in the field.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: We never yet made doubt but Rome was ready

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: To answer us.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Nor did you think it folly

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: To keep your great pretences veiled till when

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: They needs must show themselves, which, in the hatching,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: It seemed, appeared to Rome. By the discovery

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: We shall be shortened in our aim, which was

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: To take in many towns ere almost Rome

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Should know we were afoot.

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Noble Aufidius,

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Take your commission; hie you to your bands.

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Let us alone to guard Corioles.

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: If they set down before’s, for the remove

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Bring up your army. But I think you’ll find

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: They’ve not prepared for us.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: O, doubt not that;

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I speak from certainties. Nay, more,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Some parcels of their power are forth already,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And only hitherward. I leave your Honours.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: If we and Caius Martius chance to meet,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: ’Tis sworn between us we shall ever strike

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Till one can do no more.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: The gods assist you!

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And keep your Honours safe!

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Farewell.

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Farewell.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Farewell.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rome. An apartment in Martius’ house

lines.text: Enter Volumnia and Virgilia, mother and wife to Martius. They set them down on two low stools and sew.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: I pray you, daughter, sing, or express yourself in a more comfortable

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: sort. If my son were my husband, I should freelier rejoice in that

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: absence wherein he won honour than in the embracements of his bed where

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: he would show most love. When yet he was but tender-bodied and the only

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: son of my womb, when youth with comeliness plucked all gaze his way,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: when for a day of kings’ entreaties a mother should not sell him an

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: hour from her beholding, I, considering how honour would become such a

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: person—that it was no better than picture-like to hang by th’ wall, if

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: renown made it not stir—was pleased to let him seek danger where he was

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: like to find fame. To a cruel war I sent him, from whence he returned,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: his brows bound with oak. I tell thee, daughter, I sprang not more in

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: joy at first hearing he was a man-child than now in first seeing he had

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: proved himself a man.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: But had he died in the business, madam, how then?

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Then his good report should have been my son; I therein would have

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: found issue. Hear me profess sincerely: had I a dozen sons, each in my

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: love alike and none less dear than thine and my good Martius, I had

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: rather had eleven die nobly for their country than one voluptuously

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: surfeit out of action.
Enter a Gentlewoman.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Madam, the Lady Valeria is come to visit you.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: Beseech you, give me leave to retire myself.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Indeed you shall not.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Methinks I hear hither your husband’s drum,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: See him pluck Aufidius down by th’ hair;

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: As children from a bear, the Volsces shunning him.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Methinks I see him stamp thus and call thus:

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: “Come on, you cowards! You were got in fear,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Though you were born in Rome.” His bloody brow

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: With his mailed hand then wiping, forth he goes

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Like to a harvestman that’s tasked to mow

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Or all or lose his hire.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: His bloody brow? O Jupiter, no blood!

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Away, you fool! It more becomes a man

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Than gilt his trophy. The breasts of Hecuba,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: When she did suckle Hector, looked not lovelier

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Than Hector’s forehead when it spit forth blood

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: At Grecian sword, contemning.—Tell Valeria

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: We are fit to bid her welcome.
[_Exit Gentlewoman._]

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: Heavens bless my lord from fell Aufidius!

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: He’ll beat Aufidius’ head below his knee

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: And tread upon his neck.
Enter Valeria with an Usher and a Gentlewoman.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: My ladies both, good day to you.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Sweet madam.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: I am glad to see your Ladyship.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: How do you both? You are manifest housekeepers. What are you sewing

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: here? A fine spot, in good faith. How does your little son?

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: I thank your Ladyship; well, good madam.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: He had rather see the swords and hear a drum than look upon his

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: schoolmaster.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: O’ my word, the father’s son! I’ll swear ’tis a very pretty boy. O’ my

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: troth, I looked upon him o’ Wednesday half an hour together. H’as such

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: a confirmed countenance. I saw him run after a gilded butterfly, and

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: when he caught it, he let it go again, and after it again, and over and

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: over he comes, and up again, catched it again. Or whether his fall

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: enraged him or how ’twas, he did so set his teeth and tear it. O, I

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: warrant how he mammocked it!

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: One on’s father’s moods.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Indeed, la, ’tis a noble child.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: A crack, madam.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Come, lay aside your stitchery. I must have you play the idle huswife

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: with me this afternoon.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: No, good madam, I will not out of doors.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Not out of doors?

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: She shall, she shall.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: Indeed, no, by your patience. I’ll not over the threshold till my lord

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: return from the wars.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Fie, you confine yourself most unreasonably. Come, you must go visit

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: the good lady that lies in.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: I will wish her speedy strength and visit her with my prayers, but I

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: cannot go thither.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Why, I pray you?

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: ’Tis not to save labour, nor that I want love.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: You would be another Penelope. Yet they say all the yarn she spun in

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Ulysses’ absence did but fill Ithaca full of moths. Come, I would your

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: cambric were sensible as your finger, that you might leave pricking it

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: for pity. Come, you shall go with us.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: No, good madam, pardon me; indeed, I will not forth.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: In truth, la, go with me, and I’ll tell you excellent news of your

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: husband.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: O, good madam, there can be none yet.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Verily, I do not jest with you. There came news from him last night.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: Indeed, madam!

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: In earnest, it’s true. I heard a senator speak it. Thus it is: the

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Volsces have an army forth, against whom Cominius the General is gone

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: with one part of our Roman power. Your lord and Titus Lartius are set

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: down before their city Corioles. They nothing doubt prevailing, and to

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: make it brief wars. This is true, on mine honour, and so, I pray, go

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: with us.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: Give me excuse, good madam. I will obey you in everything hereafter.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Let her alone, lady. As she is now, she will but disease our better

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: mirth.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: In troth, I think she would.—Fare you well, then.—Come, good sweet

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: lady.—Prithee, Virgilia, turn thy solemness out o’ door, and go along

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: with us.

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: No, at a word, madam. Indeed I must not. I wish you much mirth.

lines.speaker: VALERIA
lines.text: Well then, farewell.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Martius, Titus Lartius, with drum and colours, with Captains and Soldiers, as before the city of Corioles. To them a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Yonder comes news. A wager they have met.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: My horse to yours, no.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: ’Tis done.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Agreed.
[_To Messenger_.]

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Say, has our general met the enemy?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: They lie in view but have not spoke as yet.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: So the good horse is mine.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: I’ll buy him of you.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: No, I’ll nor sell nor give him. Lend you him I will

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: For half a hundred years.—Summon the town.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: How far off lie these armies?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Within this mile and half.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Then shall we hear their ’larum, and they ours.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Now, Mars, I prithee, make us quick in work,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That we with smoking swords may march from hence

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To help our fielded friends!—Come, blow thy blast.
[_They sound a parley._]
Enter two Senators with others on the walls of Corioles.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Tullus Aufidius, is he within your walls?

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: No, nor a man that fears you less than he:

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: That’s lesser than a little.
[_Drum afar off_.]

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Hark, our drums

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Are bringing forth our youth. We’ll break our walls

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Rather than they shall pound us up. Our gates,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Which yet seem shut, we have but pinned with rushes.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: They’ll open of themselves.
[_Alarum far off_.]

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Hark you, far off!

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: There is Aufidius. List what work he makes

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Amongst your cloven army.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: O, they are at it!

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Their noise be our instruction.—Ladders, ho!
Enter the Army of the Volsces as through the city gates.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They fear us not but issue forth their city.—

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Now put your shields before your hearts, and fight

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: With hearts more proof than shields.—Advance, brave Titus.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: They do disdain us much beyond our thoughts,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Which makes me sweat with wrath.—Come on, my fellows!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: He that retires, I’ll take him for a Volsce,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And he shall feel mine edge.
[_Alarums. The Romans are beat back to their trenches. They exit, with the Volsces following_.]
Enter Martius cursing, with Roman soldiers.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: All the contagion of the south light on you,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: You shames of Rome! You herd of—Boils and plagues

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Plaster you o’er, that you may be abhorred

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Farther than seen, and one infect another

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Against the wind a mile! You souls of geese,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: That bear the shapes of men, how have you run

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: From slaves that apes would beat! Pluto and hell!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: All hurt behind. Backs red, and faces pale

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: With flight and agued fear! Mend, and charge home,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Or, by the fires of heaven, I’ll leave the foe

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And make my wars on you. Look to’t. Come on!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: If you’ll stand fast we’ll beat them to their wives,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: As they us to our trenches. Follow’s!
[_Another alarum. The Volsces re-enter and are driven back to the gates of Corioles, which open to admit them._]

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: So, now the gates are ope. Now prove good seconds!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: ’Tis for the followers fortune widens them,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Not for the fliers. Mark me, and do the like.
[_Martius follows the fleeing Volsces through the gates, and is shut in._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Foolhardiness, not I.

lines.speaker: SECOND SOLDIER
lines.text: Nor I.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: See, they have shut him in.
[_Alarum continues._]

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: To th’ pot, I warrant him.
Enter Titus Lartius.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: What is become of Martius?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Slain, sir, doubtless.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Following the fliers at the very heels,

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: With them he enters, who upon the sudden

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Clapped to their gates. He is himself alone,

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: To answer all the city.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: O noble fellow,

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Who sensibly outdares his senseless sword,

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: And when it bows, stand’st up! Thou art left, Martius.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: A carbuncle entire, as big as thou art,

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Were not so rich a jewel. Thou wast a soldier

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Even to Cato’s wish, not fierce and terrible

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Only in strokes, but with thy grim looks and

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: The thunderlike percussion of thy sounds

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Thou mad’st thine enemies shake, as if the world

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Were feverous and did tremble.
Enter Martius, bleeding, assaulted by the enemy.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Look, sir.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: O, ’tis Martius!

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Let’s fetch him off or make remain alike.
[_They fight, and all enter the city._]
Enter certain Romans, with spoils.

lines.speaker: FIRST ROMAN
lines.text: This will I carry to Rome.

lines.speaker: SECOND ROMAN
lines.text: And I this.

lines.speaker: THIRD ROMAN
lines.text: A murrain on’t! I took this for silver.
Enter Martius and Titus Lartius with a Trumpet.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: See here these movers that do prize their hours

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: At a cracked drachma. Cushions, leaden spoons,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Irons of a doit, doublets that hangmen would

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Bury with those that wore them, these base slaves,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Ere yet the fight be done, pack up. Down with them!
[_Exit the Romans with spoils._]
[_Alarum continues still afar off._]

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: And hark, what noise the General makes! To him!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: There is the man of my soul’s hate, Aufidius,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Piercing our Romans. Then, valiant Titus, take

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Convenient numbers to make good the city,

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Whilst I, with those that have the spirit, will haste

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: To help Cominius.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Worthy sir, thou bleed’st.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Thy exercise hath been too violent

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: For a second course of fight.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Sir, praise me not.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: My work hath yet not warmed me. Fare you well.

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: The blood I drop is rather physical

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Than dangerous to me. To Aufidius thus

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: I will appear and fight.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Now the fair goddess Fortune

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Fall deep in love with thee, and her great charms

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Misguide thy opposers’ swords! Bold gentleman,

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Prosperity be thy page!

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Thy friend no less

lines.speaker: MARTIUS
lines.text: Than those she placeth highest! So farewell.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Thou worthiest Martius!
[_Exit Martius._]

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Go sound thy trumpet in the marketplace.

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Call thither all the officers o’ th’ town,

lines.speaker: LARTIUS
lines.text: Where they shall know our mind. Away!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Cominius as it were in retire, with Soldiers.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Breathe you, my friends. Well fought! We are come off

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Like Romans, neither foolish in our stands

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Nor cowardly in retire. Believe me, sirs,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: We shall be charged again. Whiles we have struck,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: By interims and conveying gusts we have heard

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: The charges of our friends. The Roman gods

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Lead their successes as we wish our own,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: That both our powers, with smiling fronts encount’ring,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: May give you thankful sacrifice!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Thy news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The citizens of Corioles have issued,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And given to Lartius and to Martius battle.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I saw our party to their trenches driven,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And then I came away.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Though thou speakest truth,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Methinks thou speak’st not well. How long is’t since?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Above an hour, my lord.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: ’Tis not a mile; briefly we heard their drums.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: How couldst thou in a mile confound an hour

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: And bring thy news so late?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Spies of the Volsces

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Held me in chase, that I was forced to wheel

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Three or four miles about; else had I, sir,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Half an hour since brought my report.
[_Exit Messenger._]
Enter Martius, bloody.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Who’s yonder,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
