lines.text: I’ th’ absence of the needer.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Fare ye well.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Thou hast years upon thee, and thou art too full

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Of the wars’ surfeits to go rove with one

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: That’s yet unbruised. Bring me but out at gate.—

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Come, my sweet wife, my dearest mother, and

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: My friends of noble touch. When I am forth,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Bid me farewell, and smile. I pray you, come.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: While I remain above the ground, you shall

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Hear from me still, and never of me aught

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: But what is like me formerly.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: That’s worthily

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: As any ear can hear. Come, let’s not weep.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: If I could shake off but one seven years

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: From these old arms and legs, by the good gods,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: I’d with thee every foot.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Give me thy hand.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Come.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rome. A street near the gate

lines.text: Enter two Tribunes, Sicinius, Brutus with the Aedile.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Bid them all home. He’s gone, and we’ll no further.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: The nobility are vexed, whom we see have sided

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: In his behalf.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Now we have shown our power,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let us seem humbler after it is done

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Than when it was a-doing.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Bid them home.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Say their great enemy is gone, and they

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Stand in their ancient strength.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Dismiss them home.
[_Exit Aedile._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Here comes his mother.
Enter Volumnia, Virgilia and Menenius.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Let’s not meet her.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: They say she’s mad.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: They have ta’en note of us. Keep on your way.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: O, you’re well met. The hoarded plague o’ th’ gods

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Requite your love!

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Peace, peace! Be not so loud.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: If that I could for weeping, you should hear—

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Nay, and you shall hear some. [_To Sicinius_.] Will you be gone?
[_To Brutus_.]

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: You shall stay too. I would I had the power

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: To say so to my husband.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Are you mankind?

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Ay, fool, is that a shame? Note but this, fool.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Was not a man my father? Hadst thou foxship

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: To banish him that struck more blows for Rome

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Than thou hast spoken words?

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: O blessed heavens!

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: More noble blows than ever thou wise words,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: And for Rome’s good. I’ll tell thee what—yet go.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Nay, but thou shalt stay too. I would my son

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Were in Arabia and thy tribe before him,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: His good sword in his hand.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: What then?

lines.speaker: VIRGILIA
lines.text: He’d make an end of thy posterity.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Bastards and all.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Good man, the wounds that he does bear for Rome!

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Come, come, peace.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: I would he had continued to his country

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: As he began, and not unknit himself

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: The noble knot he made.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I would he had.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: “I would he had?” ’Twas you incensed the rabble.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Cats, that can judge as fitly of his worth

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: As I can of those mysteries which heaven

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Will not have Earth to know.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Pray, let’s go.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Now, pray, sir, get you gone.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: You have done a brave deed. Ere you go, hear this:

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: As far as doth the Capitol exceed

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: The meanest house in Rome, so far my son—

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: This lady’s husband here, this, do you see?—

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Whom you have banished, does exceed you all.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Well, well, we’ll leave you.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Why stay we to be baited

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: With one that wants her wits?
[_Exeunt Tribunes._]

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Take my prayers with you.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: I would the gods had nothing else to do

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: But to confirm my curses. Could I meet ’em

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: But once a day, it would unclog my heart

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Of what lies heavy to’t.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You have told them home,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And, by my troth, you have cause. You’ll sup with me?

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Anger’s my meat. I sup upon myself

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: And so shall starve with feeding. Come, let’s go.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: Leave this faint puling, and lament as I do,

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIA
lines.text: In anger, Juno-like. Come, come, come.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Fie, fie, fie!
[_Exit Menenius._]

scenes.setting: A highway between Rome and Antium

lines.text: Enter a Roman and a Volsce.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: I know you well, sir, and you know me. Your name I think is Adrian.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: It is so, sir. Truly, I have forgot you.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: I am a Roman, and my services are, as you are, against ’em. Know you me

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: yet?

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: Nicanor, no?

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: The same, sir.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: You had more beard when I last saw you, but your favour is well

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: approved by your tongue. What’s the news in Rome? I have a note from

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: the Volscian state to find you out there. You have well saved me a

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: day’s journey.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: There hath been in Rome strange insurrections, the people against the

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: senators, patricians, and nobles.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: Hath been? Is it ended, then? Our state thinks not so. They are in a

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: most warlike preparation and hope to come upon them in the heat of

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: their division.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: The main blaze of it is past, but a small thing would make it flame

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: again; for the nobles receive so to heart the banishment of that worthy

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: Coriolanus that they are in a ripe aptness to take all power from the

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: people and to pluck from them their tribunes for ever. This lies

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: glowing, I can tell you, and is almost mature for the violent breaking

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: out.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: Coriolanus banished?

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: Banished, sir.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: You will be welcome with this intelligence, Nicanor.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: The day serves well for them now. I have heard it said the fittest time

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: to corrupt a man’s wife is when she’s fallen out with her husband. Your

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: noble Tullus Aufidius will appear well in these wars, his great opposer

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: Coriolanus being now in no request of his country.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: He cannot choose. I am most fortunate thus accidentally to encounter

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: you. You have ended my business, and I will merrily accompany you home.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: I shall between this and supper tell you most strange things from Rome,

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: all tending to the good of their adversaries. Have you an army ready,

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: say you?

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: A most royal one. The centurions and their charges, distinctly

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: billeted, already in th’ entertainment, and to be on foot at an hour’s

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: warning.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: I am joyful to hear of their readiness and am the man, I think, that

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: shall set them in present action. So, sir, heartily well met, and most

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: glad of your company.

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: You take my part from me, sir. I have the most cause to be glad of

lines.speaker: VOLSCE
lines.text: yours.

lines.speaker: ROMAN
lines.text: Well, let us go together.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Coriolanus in mean apparel, disguised and muffled.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: A goodly city is this Antium. City,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: ’Tis I that made thy widows. Many an heir

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Of these fair edifices ’fore my wars

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Have I heard groan and drop. Then know me not,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Lest that thy wives with spits and boys with stones

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: In puny battle slay me.
Enter a Citizen.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Save you, sir.

lines.speaker: CITIZEN
lines.text: And you.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Direct me, if it be your will,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Where great Aufidius lies. Is he in Antium?

lines.speaker: CITIZEN
lines.text: He is, and feasts the nobles of the state

lines.speaker: CITIZEN
lines.text: At his house this night.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Which is his house, beseech you?

lines.speaker: CITIZEN
lines.text: This here before you.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Thank you, sir. Farewell.
[_Exit Citizen._]

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: O world, thy slippery turns! Friends now fast sworn,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Whose double bosoms seems to wear one heart,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Whose hours, whose bed, whose meal and exercise

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Are still together, who twin, as ’twere, in love

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Unseparable, shall within this hour,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: On a dissension of a doit, break out

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: To bitterest enmity; so fellest foes,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Whose passions and whose plots have broke their sleep

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: To take the one the other, by some chance,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Some trick not worth an egg, shall grow dear friends

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: And interjoin their issues. So with me:

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: My birthplace hate I, and my love’s upon

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: This enemy town. I’ll enter. If he slay me,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: He does fair justice; if he give me way,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: I’ll do his country service.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Antium. A hall in Aufidius’s house

lines.text: Music plays. Enter a Servingman.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Wine, wine, wine! What service is here? I think our fellows are asleep.
[_Exit._]
Enter another Servingman.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Where’s Cotus? My master calls for him. Cotus!
[_Exit._]
Enter Coriolanus.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: A goodly house. The feast smells well, but I

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Appear not like a guest.
Enter the First Servingman.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What would you have, friend? Whence are you? Here’s no place for you.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Pray go to the door.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: I have deserved no better entertainment

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: In being Coriolanus.
Enter Second Servingman.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Whence are you, sir?—Has the porter his eyes in his head, that he gives

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: entrance to such companions?—Pray, get you out.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Away!

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Away? Get you away.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Now th’ art troublesome.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Are you so brave? I’ll have you talked with anon.
Enter Third  Servingman; the First, entering, meets him.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What fellow’s this?

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: A strange one as ever I looked on. I cannot get him out o’ th’ house.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Prithee call my master to him.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What have you to do here, fellow? Pray you, avoid the house.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Let me but stand. I will not hurt your hearth.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What are you?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: A gentleman.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: A marv’llous poor one.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: True, so I am.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Pray you, poor gentleman, take up some other station. Here’s no place

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: for you. Pray you, avoid. Come.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Follow your function, go, and batten on cold bits.
[_Pushes him away from him_.]

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What, you will not?—Prithee, tell my master what a strange guest he has

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: here.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: And I shall.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Where dwell’st thou?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Under the canopy.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Under the canopy?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Where’s that?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: I’ th’ city of kites and crows.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: I’ th’ city of kites and crows? What an ass it is! Then thou dwell’st

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: with daws too?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: No, I serve not thy master.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: How, sir? Do you meddle with my master?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Ay, ’tis an honester service than to meddle with thy mistress. Thou

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: prat’st and prat’st. Serve with thy trencher, hence!
[_Beats him away_.]
[_Exit Third Servingman._]
Enter Aufidius with the Second Servingman.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Where is this fellow?

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Here, sir. I’d have beaten him like a dog, but for disturbing the lords

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: within.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Whence com’st thou? What wouldst thou?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Thy name? Why speak’st not? Speak, man. What’s thy name?
[_Removing his muffler_.]

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: If, Tullus,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Not yet thou know’st me, and, seeing me, dost not

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Think me for the man I am, necessity

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Commands me name myself.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: What is thy name?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: A name unmusical to the Volscians’ ears

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: And harsh in sound to thine.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Say, what’s thy name?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Thou has a grim appearance, and thy face

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Bears a command in’t. Though thy tackle’s torn,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Thou show’st a noble vessel. What’s thy name?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Prepare thy brow to frown. Know’st thou me yet?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I know thee not. Thy name?

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: My name is Caius Martius, who hath done

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: To thee particularly and to all the Volsces

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Great hurt and mischief; thereto witness may

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: My surname Coriolanus. The painful service,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: The extreme dangers, and the drops of blood

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Shed for my thankless country are requited

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: But with that surname, a good memory

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: And witness of the malice and displeasure

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Which thou shouldst bear me. Only that name remains.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: The cruelty and envy of the people,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Permitted by our dastard nobles, who

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Have all forsook me, hath devoured the rest,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: And suffered me by th’ voice of slaves to be

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Whooped out of Rome. Now this extremity

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Hath brought me to thy hearth, not out of hope—

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Mistake me not—to save my life; for if

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: I had feared death, of all the men i’ th’ world

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: I would have ’voided thee, but in mere spite,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: To be full quit of those my banishers,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Stand I before thee here. Then if thou hast

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: A heart of wreak in thee, that wilt revenge

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Thine own particular wrongs and stop those maims

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Of shame seen through thy country, speed thee straight

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: And make my misery serve thy turn. So use it

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: That my revengeful services may prove

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: As benefits to thee, for I will fight

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Against my cankered country with the spleen

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Of all the under fiends. But if so be

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Thou dar’st not this, and that to prove more fortunes

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Thou ’rt tired, then, in a word, I also am

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Longer to live most weary, and present

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: My throat to thee and to thy ancient malice,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Which not to cut would show thee but a fool,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Since I have ever followed thee with hate,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Drawn tuns of blood out of thy country’s breast,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: And cannot live but to thy shame, unless

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: It be to do thee service.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: O Martius, Martius,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Each word thou hast spoke hath weeded from my heart

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: A root of ancient envy. If Jupiter

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Should from yond cloud speak divine things

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And say ’tis true, I’d not believe them more

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Than thee, all-noble Martius. Let me twine

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Mine arms about that body, whereagainst

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: My grained ash an hundred times hath broke

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And scarred the moon with splinters. Here I clip

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: The anvil of my sword and do contest

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: As hotly and as nobly with thy love

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: As ever in ambitious strength I did

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Contend against thy valour. Know thou first,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I loved the maid I married; never man

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Sighed truer breath. But that I see thee here,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Thou noble thing, more dances my rapt heart

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Than when I first my wedded mistress saw

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Bestride my threshold. Why, thou Mars, I tell thee

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: We have a power on foot, and I had purpose

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Once more to hew thy target from thy brawn

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Or lose mine arm for’t. Thou hast beat me out

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Twelve several times, and I have nightly since

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Dreamt of encounters ’twixt thyself and me;

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: We have been down together in my sleep,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Unbuckling helms, fisting each other’s throat,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And waked half dead with nothing. Worthy Martius,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Had we no other quarrel else to Rome but that

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Thou art thence banished, we would muster all

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: From twelve to seventy and, pouring war

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Into the bowels of ungrateful Rome,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Like a bold flood o’erbear ’t. O, come, go in,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And take our friendly senators by th’ hands,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Who now are here, taking their leaves of me,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Who am prepared against your territories,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Though not for Rome itself.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: You bless me, gods!

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Therefore, most absolute sir, if thou wilt have

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: The leading of thine own revenges, take

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Th’ one half of my commission and set down—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: As best thou art experienced, since thou know’st

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Thy country’s strength and weakness—thine own ways,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Whether to knock against the gates of Rome,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Or rudely visit them in parts remote

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: To fright them ere destroy. But come in.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Let me commend thee first to those that shall

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Say yea to thy desires. A thousand welcomes!

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And more a friend than e’er an enemy—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Yet, Martius, that was much. Your hand. Most welcome!
[_Exeunt Coriolanus and Aufidius._]

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Two of the Servingmen come forward.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Here’s a strange alteration!

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: By my hand, I had thought to have strucken him with a cudgel, and yet

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: my mind gave me his clothes made a false report of him.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What an arm he has! He turned me about with his finger and his thumb as

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: one would set up a top.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Nay, I knew by his face that there was something in him. He had, sir, a

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: kind of face, methought—I cannot tell how to term it.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: He had so, looking as it were—Would I were hanged, but I thought there

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: was more in him than I could think.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: So did I, I’ll be sworn. He is simply the rarest man i’ th’ world.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: I think he is. But a greater soldier than he you wot one.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Who, my master?

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Nay, it’s no matter for that.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Worth six on him.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Nay, not so neither. But I take him to be the greater soldier.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Faith, look you, one cannot tell how to say that. For the defence of a

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: town our general is excellent.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Ay, and for an assault too.
Enter the Third Servingman.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: O slaves, I can tell you news, news, you rascals!

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: FIRST and SECOND SERVINGMAN.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: What, what, what? Let’s partake.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: I would not be a Roman, of all nations; I had as lief be a condemned

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: man.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: FIRST and SECOND SERVINGMAN.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Wherefore? Wherefore?

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Why, here’s he that was wont to thwack our general, Caius Martius.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Why do you say, “thwack our general”?

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: I do not say “thwack our general,” but he was always good enough for

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: him.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Come, we are fellows and friends. He was ever too hard for him; I have

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: heard him say so himself.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: He was too hard for him directly, to say the troth on’t, before

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Corioles; he scotched him and notched him like a carbonado.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: An he had been cannibally given, he might have boiled and eaten him

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: too.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: But, more of thy news?

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Why, he is so made on here within as if he were son and heir to Mars;

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: set at upper end o’ th’ table; no question asked him by any of the

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: senators but they stand bald before him. Our general himself makes a

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: mistress of him, sanctifies himself with’s hand, and turns up the white

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: o’ th’ eye to his discourse. But the bottom of the news is, our general

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: is cut i’ th’ middle and but one half of what he was yesterday, for the

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: other has half, by the entreaty and grant of the whole table. He’ll go,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: he says, and sowl the porter of Rome gates by th’ ears. He will mow all

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: down before him and leave his passage polled.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: And he’s as like to do’t as any man I can imagine.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Do’t? He will do’t! For look you, sir, he has as many friends as

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: enemies, which friends, sir, as it were, durst not, look you, sir, show

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: themselves, as we term it, his friends whilest he’s in directitude.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Directitude? What’s that?

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: But when they shall see, sir, his crest up again, and the man in blood,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: they will out of their burrows like coneys after rain, and revel all

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: with him.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: But when goes this forward?

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Tomorrow, today, presently. You shall have the drum struck up this

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: afternoon. ’Tis as it were parcel of their feast, and to be executed

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: ere they wipe their lips.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Why then, we shall have a stirring world again. This peace is nothing

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: but to rust iron, increase tailors, and breed ballad-makers.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Let me have war, say I. It exceeds peace as far as day does night. It’s

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: sprightly walking, audible, and full of vent. Peace is a very apoplexy,

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: lethargy; mulled, deaf, sleepy, insensible; a getter of more bastard

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: children than war’s a destroyer of men.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: ’Tis so, and as war in some sort, may be said to be a ravisher, so it

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: cannot be denied but peace is a great maker of cuckolds.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Ay, and it makes men hate one another.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Reason: because they then less need one another. The wars for my money!

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: I hope to see Romans as cheap as Volscians. They are rising; they are

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: rising.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: In, in, in, in!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the two Tribunes. Sicinius and Brutus.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: We hear not of him, neither need we fear him.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: His remedies are tame—the present peace,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: And quietness of the people, which before

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Were in wild hurry. Here do we make his friends

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Blush that the world goes well, who rather had,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Though they themselves did suffer by’t, behold

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Dissentious numbers pest’ring streets than see

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Our tradesmen singing in their shops and going

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: About their functions friendly.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: We stood to’t in good time.
Enter Menenius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Is this Menenius?

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: ’Tis he, ’tis he. O, he is grown most kind

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Of late.—Hail, sir!

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Hail to you both.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Your Coriolanus is not much missed

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: But with his friends. The commonwealth doth stand,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: And so would do were he more angry at it.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: All’s well, and might have been much better if

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: He could have temporized.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Where is he, hear you?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Nay, I hear nothing;

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: His mother and his wife hear nothing from him.
Enter three or four Citizens.

lines.speaker: ALL CITIZENS
lines.text: The gods preserve you both!

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Good e’en, our neighbours.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good e’en to you all, good e’en to you all.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Ourselves, our wives, and children, on our knees

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Are bound to pray for you both.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Live and thrive!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Farewell, kind neighbours. We wished Coriolanus

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Had loved you as we did.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Now the gods keep you!

lines.speaker: BOTH TRIBUNES
lines.text: Farewell, farewell.
[_Exeunt Citizens._]

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: This is a happier and more comely time

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Than when these fellows ran about the streets

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Crying confusion.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Caius Martius was

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: A worthy officer i’ th’ war, but insolent,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O’ercome with pride, ambitious, past all thinking

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Self-loving.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: And affecting one sole throne, without assistance.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: I think not so.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: We should by this, to all our lamentation,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: If he had gone forth consul, found it so.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The gods have well prevented it, and Rome

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Sits safe and still without him.
Enter an Aedile.

lines.speaker: AEDILE
lines.text: Worthy tribunes,

lines.speaker: AEDILE
lines.text: There is a slave, whom we have put in prison,

lines.speaker: AEDILE
lines.text: Reports the Volsces with two several powers

lines.speaker: AEDILE
lines.text: Are entered in the Roman territories,

lines.speaker: AEDILE
lines.text: And with the deepest malice of the war

lines.speaker: AEDILE
lines.text: Destroy what lies before ’em.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: ’Tis Aufidius,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Who, hearing of our Martius’ banishment,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Thrusts forth his horns again into the world,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Which were inshelled when Martius stood for Rome,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And durst not once peep out.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Come, what talk you of Martius?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Go see this rumourer whipped. It cannot be

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The Volsces dare break with us.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Cannot be?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: We have record that very well it can,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And three examples of the like hath been

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Within my age. But reason with the fellow

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Before you punish him, where he heard this,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Lest you shall chance to whip your information

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And beat the messenger who bids beware

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Of what is to be dreaded.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Tell not me.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: I know this cannot be.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Not possible.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The nobles in great earnestness are going

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: All to the Senate House. Some news is coming

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: That turns their countenances.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: ’Tis this slave—

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Go whip him ’fore the people’s eyes—his raising,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Nothing but his report.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Yes, worthy sir,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The slave’s report is seconded, and more,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: More fearful, is delivered.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: What more fearful?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: It is spoke freely out of many mouths—

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: How probable I do not know—that Martius,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Joined with Aufidius, leads a power ’gainst Rome

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And vows revenge as spacious as between

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The young’st and oldest thing.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: This is most likely!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Raised only that the weaker sort may wish

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good Martius home again.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: The very trick on ’t.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: This is unlikely;

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: He and Aufidius can no more atone

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Than violent’st contrariety.
Enter a Second Messenger.

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: You are sent for to the Senate.

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: A fearful army, led by Caius Martius

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: Associated with Aufidius, rages

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: Upon our territories, and have already

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: O’erborne their way, consumed with fire and took

lines.speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
lines.text: What lay before them.
Enter Cominius.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: O, you have made good work!

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: What news? What news?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: You have holp to ravish your own daughters and

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: To melt the city leads upon your pates,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: To see your wives dishonoured to your noses—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: What’s the news? What’s the news?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Your temples burned in their cement, and

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Your franchises, whereon you stood, confined

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Into an auger’s bore.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Pray now, your news?—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You have made fair work, I fear me.—Pray, your news?

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: If Martius should be joined with Volscians—

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: If?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: He is their god; he leads them like a thing

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Made by some other deity than Nature,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: That shapes man better; and they follow him

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Against us brats with no less confidence

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Than boys pursuing summer butterflies

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Or butchers killing flies.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You have made good work,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You and your apron-men, you that stood so much

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Upon the voice of occupation and

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The breath of garlic eaters!

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: He’ll shake your Rome about your ears.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: As Hercules did shake down mellow fruit.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You have made fair work.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But is this true, sir?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Ay, and you’ll look pale

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Before you find it other. All the regions

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Do smilingly revolt, and who resists

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Are mocked for valiant ignorance

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: And perish constant fools. Who is’t can blame him?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Your enemies and his find something in him.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: We are all undone unless

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: The noble man have mercy.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Who shall ask it?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: The Tribunes cannot do’t for shame; the people

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Deserve such pity of him as the wolf

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Does of the shepherds. For his best friends, if they

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Should say “Be good to Rome,” they charged him even

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: As those should do that had deserved his hate

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: And therein showed like enemies.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: ’Tis true.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: If he were putting to my house the brand

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: That should consume it, I have not the face

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: To say “Beseech you, cease.”—You have made fair hands,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You and your crafts! You have crafted fair!

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: You have brought

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: A trembling upon Rome such as was never

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: S’ incapable of help.

lines.speaker: TRIBUNES
lines.text: Say not we brought it.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: How? Was it we? We loved him, but like beasts

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And cowardly nobles, gave way unto your clusters,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Who did hoot him out o’ th’ city.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: But I fear

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: They’ll roar him in again. Tullus Aufidius,

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: The second name of men, obeys his points

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: As if he were his officer. Desperation

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: Is all the policy, strength, and defence

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: That Rome can make against them.
Enter a troop of Citizens.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Here comes the clusters.—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And is Aufidius with him? You are they

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: That made the air unwholesome when you cast

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Your stinking, greasy caps in hooting at

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Coriolanus’ exile. Now he’s coming,

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And not a hair upon a soldier’s head

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Which will not prove a whip. As many coxcombs

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: As you threw caps up will he tumble down

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: And pay you for your voices. ’Tis no matter.

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: If he could burn us all into one coal

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: We have deserved it.

lines.speaker: ALL CITIZENS
lines.text: Faith, we hear fearful news.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: For mine own part,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: When I said banish him, I said ’twas pity.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: And so did I.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: And so did I. And, to say the truth, so did very many of us. That we

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: did we did for the best; and though we willingly consented to his

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: banishment, yet it was against our will.

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: You are goodly things, you voices!

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: You have made good work, you and your cry!—

lines.speaker: MENENIUS
lines.text: Shall’s to the Capitol?

lines.speaker: COMINIUS
lines.text: O, ay, what else?
[_Exeunt Cominius and Menenius._]

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Go, masters, get you home. Be not dismayed.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: These are a side that would be glad to have

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: This true which they so seem to fear. Go home,

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: And show no sign of fear.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: The gods be good to us! Come, masters, let’s home. I ever said we were

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: i’ th’ wrong when we banished him.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: So did we all. But, come, let’s home.
[_Exeunt Citizens._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I do not like this news.

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Nor I.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let’s to the Capitol. Would half my wealth

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Would buy this for a lie!

lines.speaker: SICINIUS
lines.text: Pray let’s go.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: A camp at a short distance from Rome

lines.text: Enter Aufidius with his Lieutenant.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And my pretext to strike at him admits

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: A good construction. I raised him, and I pawned

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Mine honour for his truth, who being so heightened,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He watered his new plants with dews of flattery,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Seducing so my friends; and to this end,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He bowed his nature, never known before

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: But to be rough, unswayable, and free.

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Sir, his stoutness

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: When he did stand for consul, which he lost

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: By lack of stooping—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: That I would have spoke of.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Being banished for’t, he came unto my hearth,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Presented to my knife his throat. I took him,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Made him joint servant with me, gave him way

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: In all his own desires; nay, let him choose

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Out of my files, his projects to accomplish,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: My best and freshest men; served his designments

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: In mine own person; holp to reap the fame

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Which he did end all his; and took some pride

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: To do myself this wrong; till at the last

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I seemed his follower, not partner; and

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He waged me with his countenance as if

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I had been mercenary.

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: So he did, my lord.

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: The army marvelled at it, and, in the last,

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: When he had carried Rome and that we looked

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: For no less spoil than glory—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: There was it

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: For which my sinews shall be stretched upon him.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: At a few drops of women’s rheum, which are

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: As cheap as lies, he sold the blood and labour

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Of our great action. Therefore shall he die,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And I’ll renew me in his fall. But, hark!
[_Drums and trumpets sound, with great shouts of the people._]

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Your native town you entered like a post

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: And had no welcomes home, but he returns

lines.speaker: FIRST CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Splitting the air with noise.

lines.speaker: SECOND CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: And patient fools,

lines.speaker: SECOND CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Whose children he hath slain, their base throats tear

lines.speaker: SECOND CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: With giving him glory.

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Therefore at your vantage,

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Ere he express himself or move the people

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: With what he would say, let him feel your sword,

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: Which we will second. When he lies along,

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: After your way his tale pronounced shall bury

lines.speaker: THIRD CONSPIRATOR
lines.text: His reasons with his body.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Say no more.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Here come the lords.
Enter the Lords of the city.

lines.speaker: ALL LORDS
lines.text: You are most welcome home.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I have not deserved it.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: But, worthy lords, have you with heed perused

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: What I have written to you?

lines.speaker: ALL LORDS
lines.text: We have.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: And grieve to hear’t.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: What faults he made before the last, I think

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Might have found easy fines, but there to end

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Where he was to begin and give away

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The benefit of our levies, answering us

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: With our own charge, making a treaty where

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: There was a yielding—this admits no excuse.
Enter Coriolanus marching with Drum and Colours, the Commoners being with him.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He approaches. You shall hear him.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Hail, lords! I am returned your soldier,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: No more infected with my country’s love

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Than when I parted hence, but still subsisting

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Under your great command. You are to know

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: That prosperously I have attempted, and

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: With bloody passage led your wars even to

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: The gates of Rome. Our spoils we have brought home

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Doth more than counterpoise a full third part

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: The charges of the action. We have made peace

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: With no less honour to the Antiates

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Than shame to th’ Romans, and we here deliver,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Subscribed by th’ Consuls and patricians,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Together with the seal o’ th’ Senate, what

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: We have compounded on.
[_He offers the lords a paper._]

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Read it not, noble lords,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: But tell the traitor in the highest degree

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He hath abused your powers.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: “Traitor?” How now?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Ay, traitor, Martius.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Martius?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Ay, Martius, Caius Martius. Dost thou think

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I’ll grace thee with that robbery, thy stol’n name

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Coriolanus, in Corioles?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: You lords and heads o’ th’ state, perfidiously

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He has betrayed your business and given up

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: For certain drops of salt your city Rome—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: I say your city—to his wife and mother,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Breaking his oath and resolution like

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: A twist of rotten silk, never admitting

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Counsel o’ th’ war, but at his nurse’s tears

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: He whined and roared away your victory,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: That pages blushed at him and men of heart

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Looked wond’ring each at other.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Hear’st thou, Mars?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Name not the god, thou boy of tears.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Ha?

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: No more.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Measureless liar, thou hast made my heart

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Too great for what contains it. “Boy”? O slave!—

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Pardon me, lords, ’tis the first time that ever

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: I was forced to scold. Your judgments, my grave lords,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Must give this cur the lie; and his own notion—

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Who wears my stripes impressed upon him, that

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Must bear my beating to his grave—shall join

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: To thrust the lie unto him.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Peace, both, and hear me speak.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Cut me to pieces, Volsces. Men and lads,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Stain all your edges on me. “Boy”? False hound!

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: If you have writ your annals true, ’tis there,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: That like an eagle in a dovecote, I

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Fluttered your Volscians in Corioles,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: Alone I did it. “Boy”!

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Why, noble lords,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Will you be put in mind of his blind fortune,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Which was your shame, by this unholy braggart,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: ’Fore your own eyes and ears?

lines.speaker: ALL CONSPIRATORS
lines.text: Let him die for’t.

lines.speaker: ALL CONSPIRATORS
lines.text: ALL PEOPLE

lines.speaker: ALL CONSPIRATORS
lines.text: Tear him to pieces! Do it presently! He killed my son! My daughter! He

lines.speaker: ALL CONSPIRATORS
lines.text: killed my cousin Marcus! He killed my father!

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Peace, ho! No outrage! Peace!

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: The man is noble, and his fame folds in

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: This orb o’ th’ Earth. His last offences to us

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Shall have judicious hearing. Stand, Aufidius,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: And trouble not the peace.

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: O that I had him,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: With six Aufidiuses, or more, his tribe,

lines.speaker: CORIOLANUS
lines.text: To use my lawful sword.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Insolent villain!

lines.speaker: ALL CONSPIRATORS
lines.text: Kill, kill, kill, kill, kill him!
[_Draw the Conspirators, and kills Martius, who falls. Aufidius stands on him._]

lines.speaker: LORDS
lines.text: Hold, hold, hold, hold!

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: My noble masters, hear me speak.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: O Tullus!

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Thou hast done a deed whereat valour will weep.

lines.speaker: THIRD LORD
lines.text: Tread not upon him.—Masters, all be quiet.—

lines.speaker: THIRD LORD
lines.text: Put up your swords.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: My lords, when you shall know—as in this rage,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Provoked by him, you cannot—the great danger

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Which this man’s life did owe you, you’ll rejoice

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: That he is thus cut off. Please it your Honours

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: To call me to your senate, I’ll deliver

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Myself your loyal servant, or endure

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Your heaviest censure.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Bear from hence his body,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: And mourn you for him. Let him be regarded

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: As the most noble corse that ever herald

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Did follow to his urn.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: His own impatience

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Takes from Aufidius a great part of blame.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Let’s make the best of it.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: My rage is gone,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: And I am struck with sorrow.—Take him up.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Help, three o’ th’ chiefest soldiers; I’ll be one.—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Beat thou the drum that it speak mournfully.—

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Trail your steel pikes. Though in this city he

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Hath widowed and unchilded many a one,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Which to this hour bewail the injury,

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Yet he shall have a noble memory.

lines.speaker: AUFIDIUS
lines.text: Assist.
[_Exeunt, bearing the body of Martius. A dead march sounded._]
